note: Adjudicated variants: three of punctuation and the words of consecration in capitals (eight entries in all). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: No comma before the ac joining the second adjective, with do and with the typical edition: sanctas ac venerábiles is one pair qualifying manus.

No comma after Deum in the apposition ad te Deum Patrem suum omnipoténtem, with handmissal-eo; the comma is do's own pointing, and the corpus rules the same apposition without a comma at ordinarium.deus-qui-humanae and ordinarium.suscipe-sancta-trinitas.
Full stop closing the command to the disciples, with do and with the typical edition: what follows is not its continuation but the form of consecration, which the missal sets apart.

The words of consecration are set in the case the TYPICAL EDITION prints — Hoc est enim Corpus meum, Hic est enim Calix Sánguinis mei — with capitals only where that edition capitalises: the opening word, and Corpus, Calix and Sánguinis. Both hand missals set the whole formula in capitals, and this edition followed them until the typical edition itself could be read (leaf 386-387 of the 600 dpi scan, printed pages 306-307). The authority's own practice governs; the hand missals' capitals are recorded here rather than corrected, since neither page is wrong and the letters are identical.
